title: Piano players and bands meeting on trucks to advertise dances
summary: He recalls pianists Burnell, Little Willie and Red Caillou, and bands on trucks meeting on corners.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Well, who were the piano players? Do you remember any of them?

Well, yes. I remember a wood of them. We had some wonderful piano players. That's some of these, well, in these late years, right around here, youngsters. This boy Burnell, he's one of the best. And that boy could wake his finger like an electric piano. The dope killed him. We got another man called Little Willie. The dope killed him. See, one of the things about them, and see, if they were using the right stuff, but they would get that junk. And that junk just knocks them out. Where's Red Caillou, he was a wonderful little piano player, and they used to buck. They used to buck. They'd come in the place, five or six of them, and one off the stool, the other's on, one off the stool, the other's on, just bucking against one another. And boy, you'd be talking to something. Well we should have, we should have appetized for a dance. The bands would meet on the corner sometimes, three bands. Just stay out there an hour. Chris Kelly, Rainey, and a punch. Or Sam Morgan, Chris Kelly, and Rainey. They'd always meet, and we'll see at those times we'd have appetized for a dance. Like we were going to give a dance at the economy hall, at the car operators hall, or the France Army. They'd get a, there wasn't no trucks at that time. Yes it was trucks, that's right. They'd take a truck, put a big sign on it, and the band would be in the truck. And they'd stop at each corner and play while they got a ballroom. And they'd sometimes all meet, sometimes four bands would be on one corner. And they'd steady hours at this plane, one after another. That's why I said they don't have a time now that we hadn't, we'd come along. Because the band would, now my club was giving a dance, we'd have a time for that dance. Well yeah we'd have a time for that dance. Hire that band, hire that truck. And they'd go all around, we wouldn't go too far out of our neighborhood, you know, way uptown. We'd go around where we know it's going to bring the people that are going to come. And somebody else had got a dance, they hire a truck. And they'd all meet and they'd play out there for hours at a time. There was plenty of pleasure then. There wasn't fights like we did today, you know, killing like you do now. We just drink and have fun.
